papers.relevance: Directly informs how to preserve model quality under low-rank weight compression, though it does not train weights to become more compressible.

papers.summary: Derives how optimizer geometry changes singular-mode emergence and decay in deep matrix factorization. Controlled experiments show different transient rank trajectories even when optimizers reach similar final losses and effective ranks.
papers.relevance: Addresses whether optimization changes effective rank, but its phase laws rely on balance and alignment assumptions rather than LLM experiments.

evidence.quote: Although the methods eventually reach similar losses and effective ranks, their trajectories differ substantially.
Although the phase laws rely on balance and alignment assumptions, they identify concrete mechanisms to understand optimizer behavior.

papers.relevance: Connects LoRA rank, memorization and generalization under label noise, with a direct language-model test.

At LLaMA-1.3B, Q-Clean reports 1.28G optimizer memory and 12.10 perplexity versus Muon's 2.80G and 11.78. Clean reports reaching AdamW's final loss in 64 rather than 81 hours on four H100 GPUs.
papers.relevance: Provides measured memory, quality and wall-clock tradeoffs for memory-efficient LLM pretraining.

papers.summary: RoM optimizes LoRA updates on a fixed-rank manifold to account for factorization gauge symmetry. In a three-run Qwen2.5-3B RL comparison, it reports higher accuracy than Adam on MATH-500, GSM8K and OlympiadBench, with 1.08× end-to-end time per step.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses low-rank optimization geometry and practical language-model fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: We design our optimizer on the manifold of fixed-rank matrices, aiming to optimize the product of the low-rank factors directly rather than each factor separately.

papers.title: Rotated Manifold Optimization for Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.summary: LoRA-Norm rebalances an adapter's singular-value gains after training while preserving per-module nuclear norm. Across 18 adapters, it reports average improvements in specialization and capability retention; energy-matched controls recover much of the benefit.
papers.relevance: Tests a spectral intervention on LoRA updates, while cautioning against attributing its gains solely to spectral shape.

evidence.quote: Across 18 adapters spanning two backbones and three tasks, it improves both objectives on average.
Energy-matched controls recover much of the benefit, while stronger functional equalization yields no consistent further gains, limiting claims of an independent spectral-shape advantage.

papers.summary: Compares six retrieval strategies on a shared scientific-paper corpus and synthetic question set. ColBERT reports gold-paper Hit@3 of 92.8–94.8%, versus 47.5–52.8% for rephrasing plus reranking.
papers.relevance: Directly informs retrieval and ranking choices for a research-digest agent; the synthetic queries limit direct transfer to personalized paper selection.

evidence.quote: All six strategies were run on the same 9,742 papers for which query generation succeeded, so each strategy has 19,484 question instances and every cross-strategy comparison is paired at the query level.
ColBERT retrieves the gold paper within the top 3 for 92.8% of problem queries and 94.8% of method queries — roughly double the best single-vector pipeline (Rephrased & Reranked: 47.5% and 52.8%).
